turns.reply: The objective ('more customers using the card for online spend') is a business goal, not yet a defined behaviour or audience. Before I can pick an entry event, a goal event, or an intervention, I need three things only the business can give me: how they will judge this working, who exactly counts as the target (never used online vs. underusing), and what they believe is blocking online usage today — because each of those leads to a genuinely different campaign (different audience, different entry point, different message mechanism). I've checked what events, attributes and channels the platform actually supports so I don't design against something unbuildable, but none of that tells me which of these campaigns to build.
questions: How will you judge whether this campaign worked — e.g. a rise in the number of customers making at least one online transaction, a rise in total online spend value, or something else you track? If you don't have a formal target yet, that's fine to say.

Who should this reach: customers who have never made an online transaction with this card at all, customers who used to but have gone quiet, or active online spenders you want spending more? These are quite different audiences and journeys.

What's your best guess at what's stopping online usage — e.g. the card/account isn't enabled or activated for online use, customers don't realise they can use it online, or there's just no compelling reason/offer to switch spend to this card? If you're not sure, say so — I can design a test instead of assuming.

turns.reply: Two of the three open questions are now settled by your reply: you have no formal target yet (fine, per the question itself) and no hypothesis about the offline-vs-online driver (also anticipated — so rather than assume a cause, I'll design this as a test of competing explanations instead of betting on one). One fork is still genuinely unanswered and it is not a data question at all — it is a targeting decision only you can make, and it changes who receives messages, what the entry event is, and what the message says. I also need to flag a real platform finding before you decide: the Transaction event only exposes Transaction Type (fund-movement types like AUTHORIZE, REFUND, EMI_PRINCIPAL etc.), Transaction Status, Amount, EMI Eligible, MCC (free-form, unconstrained) and Initiated By (CUSTOMER_INITIATED / SYSTEM_GENERATED). None of these mark a transaction as 'online' vs 'offline' — there is no channel or card-present flag. So however you answer the audience question, I cannot currently prove or filter strictly on 'did this customer transact online' — only on 'did this customer transact at all.' I will carry that as a disclosed limitation either way, but it matters most for how precisely we can define 'never transacted online' vs 'used to.'
questions: Who should this campaign reach: customers who have never made an online transaction with this card at all, customers who used to but have gone quiet online, or active online spenders you want spending more? This is a pure targeting choice, independent of the data gap you mentioned — I need your intent even without numbers to back it.
